title: Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition & Billing Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's end-to-end processes for contracting, procurement, invoicing, and revenue recognition. It combines legal review and procurement controls with finance policies required for accurate and auditable revenue recognition and billing. The document is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales, and Program owners who handle vendor agreements, customer contracts, and purchase orders.

Scope:
- Applies to all third-party vendor engagements, customer commercial contracts (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and procurement activities regardless of region.
- Excludes routine employee expense reimbursements (see Expense Policy).

Key definitions:
- Customer Contract: Agreement with a customer for Redwood services (hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployments).
- Vendor Contract: Agreement with a supplier for goods or services.
- PO: Purchase Order issued by Finance/Procurement.
- Committed Capacity Contract: Customer contract that includes an upfront committed payment for Reserved (Dedicated) capacity.
- Usage Contract: Metered / per-token billing.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Legal: Contract language, risk review, non-standard clause negotiation. Owner: Legal Counsel (contracts).
- Finance: Revenue recognition, invoicing cadence, deferred revenue accounting, PO issuance. Owner: Head of Finance (Revenue Ops).
- Procurement: Vendor selection, vendor onboarding (W-9 / W-8, security questionnaire), PO enforcement. Owner: Procurement Manager.
- Sales / AE: Commercial negotiation, redlines subject to Legal & Finance approval.
- Product / Eng (if applicable): Technical requirements or SOW reviews for Private/on-prem projects.

Contract lifecycle (high-level):
1) Intake: Sales/Stakeholder uploads executed Term Sheet / commercial summary into contract-tracker and selects contract type (Standard, High-Risk, SOW, NDA).
2) Standard templates: Use Redwood standard templates located in the Contracts library. Deviations must be noted on the intake form.
3) Negotiation: Sales negotiates commercial terms. Any non-standard legal terms (indemnity, data residency, source code escrow, custom SLAs) flagged for Legal review.
4) Legal review: Legal performs clause-level review and records risk bucket (Low / Medium / High). High risk requires Legal + Head of Finance escalation.
5) Finance review: Finance validates billing model, invoicing cadence, tax implications, revenue recognition treatment.
6) Approval & Signatures: Route for approval based on approval thresholds table below. Signatures captured in DocuSign and stored in Contract Repository.
7) Post-signature: Finance creates revenue schedule in the General Ledger / RevRec tool. Procurement (if vendor) issues PO. Sales Ops tags contract metadata in CRM (customer id, product sku, effective date, term).

Approval thresholds (quick reference):
- Amounts below are total contract value (TCV) unless stated otherwise.

TCV | Required Approver(s) | Legal Review | Finance Review | Notes
- <$25k | Contracting Manager | Standard template only | Procurement sign-off if vendor | Expedited route allowed
- $25k - $250k | Director-level | Required for any deviation from template | Required | Standard SLA & revrec schedule
- $250k - $1M | VP-level | Required | Required + RevRec schedule approval | Can require executive sponsor sign-off
- > $1M | CFO + General Counsel | Required | Required + Deferred revenue model sign-off | Additional procurement/board notifications possible

Procurement procedures (vendor side):
1) Vendor selection: use approved vendor list where available. For new vendors, run vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire, SOC 2 if relevant, business continuity).
2) Competitive procurement: For purchases > $250k, run an RFP or competitive evaluation documented in the procurement folder.
3) Vendor onboarding: collect W-9/W-8, ACH or wire details, insurance certificate, and contact info. Procurement creates vendor record in ERP.
4) POs: All purchases must have an approved PO prior to work commencement unless pre-approved as non-PO spend by Procurement (exceptions recorded). POs are issued via ERP with matching to vendor invoices.
5) Invoice processing: Three-way match where applicable (PO, invoice, receiving report). Finance processes payments on standard net terms (default Net 30).

Non-PO / emergency purchases:
- Non-PO requests require written justification and Procurement Manager approval. Emergency spend > $50k requires VP approval after the fact.

Contract clauses & legal routing guidelines:
- Use standard clauses where possible. Avoid unlimited liability; cap liability to the contract value x2 unless Executive / Legal approval is obtained.
- Indemnity: Prefer mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims; customer-specific indemnity requests must be routed to Legal.
- Data residency & security: Any language changing default data residency or adding additional security obligations must be reviewed by Security + Legal.
- IP & ownership: Standard Redwood position is to retain model IP and grant customer a service license. Exceptions escalate to Legal Counsel.

Revenue recognition & billing policy summary:
- Accounting standard: Redwood follows ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent) for revenue recognition.
- Revenue models in scope:
  - Usage-based (metered API): Recognize revenue as performance obligations are satisfied (i.e., as tokens are delivered / services rendered). Invoices typically monthly in arrears; revenue recognized in the month the usage occurred.
  - Committed Capacity / Reserved (Dedicated): If customer prepays for committed capacity covering a time-bound service period, recognize as deferred revenue and amortize over the service period (straight-line unless contractually specified otherwise).
  - Term licenses / setup fees for Private deployments / on-prem: Typically bifurcate setup (performance obligation delivered at install) from recurring support (recognized over time). Finance must analyze each contract for distinct performance obligations.
  - Multi-element arrangements: Use allocation based on standalone selling prices. Document the allocation methodology in RevRec schedule.

Billing & invoicing practices:
- Invoicing cadence:
  - Usage contracts: monthly in arrears, with detailed usage CSV export attached to invoice.
  - Committed contracts: monthly or quarterly billing per commercial terms; prepaid upfront accepted but recognized over the covered term.
  - Professional services / SOW: milestone-based invoicing with acceptance criteria; copy of acceptance or sign-off required.
- Payment terms: standard Net 30. Deviations (Net 45/60) require Finance approval and are recorded in the contract metadata.
- Credits & disputes: Customers have 30 days to dispute invoice items. Process: (1) Customer opens ticket to billing@redwood.com, (2) Billing team investigates within 5 business days, (3) If credit warranted, issue credit memo and adjust next invoice or refund per policy.
- Tax & withholding: Finance determines tax treatment; for cross-border transactions, collect appropriate W-8/W-9 and apply withholding rules per jurisdiction.

Revenue close & audit evidence checklist (monthly):
- RevRec schedule updated in ERP / RevRec tool for new contract signings.
- Deferred revenue roll-forward reconciled to general ledger monthly.
- Usage invoices sampled and matched to recorded revenue.
- Contract file (signed agreement + SOW + pricing annex) attached to the contract record in the repository for audit evidence.

Templates, tools & location:
- Contract templates: /contracts/templates (Legal Confluence + Contract Repository link).
- Contract tracker: Contract-tracker (Sales Ops) - required intake form for every new customer agreement.
- RevRec tool: RevRec system name (ERP integration) - Finance maintains the definitive revenue schedule.
- Invoicing & payments: ERP Billing module; DocuSign for executed signatures.

Escalation & exceptions:
- High-risk legal language or novel commercial structures: Escalate to General Counsel and Head of Finance.
- Exceptions to PO policy or approval thresholds: Documented waiver, signed by Procurement Manager + Head of Finance.

Frequently used checklists (examples):
- Contract handoff to Finance checklist: Signed contract, effective date, TCV, billing frequency, payment terms, GL mapping, customer tax ID, sales rep, and RevRec owner.
- Vendor onboarding checklist: W-9/W-8, invoice remit details, insurance cert, SOC 2 report (if required), vendor code in ERP.

Appendix A - Example revrec treatments (short):
- Example 1 - Usage contract: Customer A consumed $12,340 in API usage in January. Invoice issued 2026-02-05 in arrears. Revenue recognized in January (month of usage).
- Example 2 - Dedicated committed contract: Customer B prepays $600,000 for 12 months of Dedicated capacity. Finance records $600,000 as deferred revenue on receipt and recognizes $50,000/month over the 12-month period.

Appendix B - Sample PO email to vendor: "Dear Vendor, please find attached PO #12345 for services beginning 2026-03-01. Please confirm receipt and earliest invoice remit instructions (ACH details preferred). Reference PO #12345 on all invoices."

Questions or suggested updates should be sent to finance-ops@redwood.com.
